steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix ground beef, bread crumbs, ketchup, eggs, soy sauce, black pepper, and garlic powder in a large bowl until well combined. Shape into small meatballs and arrange on a nonstick baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until browned, about 30 minutes, turning once.
Meanwhile, combine cranberry sauce, BBQ sauce, brown sugar, and lemon juice in a large saucepan; heat and stir over low heat until smooth. Add meatballs and simmer for I hour. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Meatballs
raw_recipe.description: These festive cranberry meatballs are made with ground beef and cooked in a cranberry sauce for a delicious Thanksgiving or Christmas appetizer.
raw_recipe.name: Cranberry Meatballs

review.reviewBody: I made with the frozen meatballs. I mixed together the sauce in the crockpot, threw in the meatballs, and set on low all day. They were fantastic! We had baked potatoes and green beans with it and it was wonderful.

This was a good recipe, although I modified it slightly. I halved the recipe as 7 portions was too much food.
In the meatball portion of the recipe, I didn't have soy sauce, so I used worcestershire sauce instead. The meatballs came out perfectly, nice and soft, and I cooked them in the oven as explained, but before I covered the meatballs with the sauce, I flipped them over, so they could be cooked evenly on both sides. Next time I would lower the temperature 25 degrees, as I used a pyrex pan.

For the sauce, instead of cranberries, I used 3/4 cup of lingonberries and 1/4 cup of blueberry preserves. I used garlic BBQ sauce and prange juice instead of lemon juice. Once the sauce simmered and then cooked on the actual meatballs, the flavours blended perfectly. I would definitely make again and perhaps attempt a version in the crockpot :)
I also made this with frozen meatballs. I defrosted the meatballs ahead of time, made the sauce as directed,added the meatballs and the sauce in the crockpot to heat them. It was a big hit!

The recipe is a great base recipe. It's good on its own really good. I make these in my ninja three in one pot. I sear the meatballs and then turn it down to slow cooker or crock pot setting after I put the sauce in. 1/2 batch perfectly covers the bottom of my ninja large pot with meatballs.. 😉 I have substituted the beef for pork burger, ground goat and even ground turkey that I grind myself at home and it is fabulous! I'm sure venison would be good in this recipe also, just don't have much of that here in Arizona... I usually use Worcestershire sauce instead of soy sauce and cracker crumbs instead of bread crumbs cuz I hardly ever have any bread crumbs around. Thanks for making this one available!!!

I was in a hurry (last-minute holiday party), so I used small, frozen meatballs, defrosted them, and threw them in a crock pot. I mixed the sauce ingredients in a saucepan, heated it and poured over the meatballs. I used 1 1/2 cans cranberry sauce and a bit less BBQ sauce (Sweet Baby Ray's) than the recipe called for, as I like a bit more of the cranberry flavor to come through. Took a box of toothpicks along to make them hors d'oeuvres for wandering partygoers and they were a hit. So yummy and easy. :)

Crowd Pleaser! I varied as follows: 1 lb grd beef, 1 lb grd turkey. Mince 1 sm onion in food processor, add the eggs, soy sauce, pepper, garlic powder, ketchup, blend well, add meats, blend well, slowly add bread crumbs (plain). Make meatballs and bake per recipe. Sauce: make as above but mix in 4 chopped green onions just prior to adding the meatballs to the sauce. Opt: sprinkle 2 T. toasted sesame seeds. YUM!

Use Costco Frozen Italian meatballs, one can of Jellied Cranberry Sauce and one bottle of Chili Sauce... That's all you need. Warm to melt cranberry sauce and mix Chili Sauce together in a pot. Add meatballs and warm through, stirring while it warms. I dump the frozen meatballs in the sauce to warm on low for a good half-hour at least.

These meatballs were good but instead of BBQ sauce I used the Heinz Chili sauce in the bottle and they turned out great. Did not cook them for 1 hour, this makes them dry and tough. I simmered them for 20 mins. and let set for 30 mins. They were great.

A pretty simple recipe, one of those easy throw together "potluck" meatball recipes. The texture was just ok; I'd probably use less bread crumbs. The sauce was easy enough and a pretty standard jelly/bbq sauce recipe. You could use the slow cooker instead of simmering on the stove. I would also cut back on the cook time in the oven - they don't need 30 minutes if they're going to then simmer an hour.

I bought frozen meatballs both beef and turkey and they came out amazing! I was hesitant about the cranberry sauce because I don't usually like it but I changed my mind once I tasted it. I changed nothing about the recipe other than using frozen meatballs and letting them sit in a crock-pot on low for a few hours. Made these 4 times in a 2 week period!

This is a pretty forgiving recipe. You can replace ingredients and adjust the recipe to your own taste and it'll be just fine. I made this for my son's preschool x-mas pot luck. But before I actually took it to the school I tried out the recipe to make sure I get it right for the actual party. I thought the sauce was just too much (too sweet and saucey). I cut bbq sauce and brown sugar to half and it was just right for me - not overrun with sauce & too sweet. I didn't have on hand of all things, ketchup. So I replaced it with some tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, and red wine vinegar. End result: We had over 20 different dishes at the pot luck - and my boy ate my meatballs and kept on eating just that. FYI he was impartial b/c it's not the normal thing I cook at home and he had no idea who cooked what... As long as my picky son was happy, I think this dish is a success. Oh I made some extra for home. I made meatball sandwiches on a baguette and it's even better on sandwiches. Thank you for the recipe!
These were a huge hit at our Christmas Eve party! Good recipe!
I had more than two pounds of meat so I added some blackberry jelly to the cranberry sauce. Added a little more lemon juice. It was really delicious and the family wants me to make them again!
This was great. Made it to use up Thanksgiving cranberry sauce. I combined ground pork and beef. Makes for a more tender meatball. Don’t pan fry before the oven. Why! You lose all the juice.
These meatballs are so good. I like to serve them over rice. Such a great recipe!
Absolutely delicious! Accidently put in a can of whole cranberries, but it was still tasty. Will definitely make these again.
Sauce was good but the texture of the meatballs was not good. It was the only appetizer left after my party
They were tasty. I used Crispy Fried Onions (gluten free), instead of bread crumbs because my granddaughter has celiac. There were none left over. Will definitely make again.
I want to try it using cranberry jelly and chill sauce, basically subbing the cran jelly for grape in the classic recipe for smokies or meatballs. Also, this begs to have turkey meatballs!

I've been making these for years and my mother, back in the late 50's, did too! Good but very sweet. It can be used with cocktail sausages or even smoked sausage cut in discs and browned before adding the sauce.
